items.title: Feral Youth Leaves Man's Intestines Hanging Out; Judge Lets Him Walk The Same Day
items.content_text:
Feral Youth Leaves Man's Intestines Hanging Out; Judge Lets Him Walk The Same Day

Authored by Steve Watson via Modernity.news,

A 19-year-old charged with stabbing a man in Pittsburgh's Garfield neighborhood, so badly that officers found the victim's intestines protruding, was released the same day on a promise to come back to court.

He did not have to post a dime. Eight days later he was the prime suspect in yet another stabbing, this one at an East Liberty bus station, and he is now charged with attempted homicide.

District Judge Dan Butler signed the non-monetary bond. Pittsburgh Police Chief Jason Lando, expressed disbelief that the suspect was walking free. This all occurred in Democrat-run Allegheny County.

A 19-year-old charged with stabbing a man in Pittsburgh so badly his intestines were hanging out was released the SAME DAY without posting a dime.

Eight days later, he's the prime suspect in ANOTHER stabbing.

District Judge Dan Butler let Delvin Dobbins walk on a non-monetary bond. Just a promise to show up to court.

Pittsburgh Police Chief Jason Lando couldn't believe he was out.

"How can that be? I mean, he just stabbed someone in the stomach a week ago."

And it's happened before.

Two years earlier, Dobbins was let go after a burglary arrest because the juvenile detention center had closed. Two months later, he was charged with SHOOTING a convenience store clerk.

Two stabbings and a shooting. The man keeps racking up victims because the judge keeps SETTING HIM LOOSE!

— The Vigilant Fox 🦊 (@VigilantFox) October 8, 2026

On September 23, police were called to the 5000 block of Penn Avenue after a fight that began on a bus. WPXI reported that officers arrived to a man whose intestines were hanging out of his body. Delvin Dobbins, 19, was chased a short distance, tased, and found with a bloodied knife. He was charged with aggravated assault. The victim was hospitalized in serious condition and survived.

Chief Lando addressed the case the next morning on local radio.

"I remember in the police report it said when the officers arrived on scene the man's intestines were protruding," Lando said. "The officers immediately began rendering aid to prevent him from bleeding out."

Incredibly, Butler released Dobbins on a non-monetary bond that same day. No cash. A signature and a date. Sources told WPXI's 11 Investigates that Butler should not have done it. The Fifth Judicial District, which oversees Allegheny County magistrates, declined to comment.

Lando said he assumed the suspect was still locked up.

"I said, how can that be? He just stabbed someone in the stomach a week ago. Surely he would still be in jail," Lando said. "And I learned that the 19-year-old from the Penn Ave. stabbing was released on a non-monetary bond, which means you basically promise that you're just going to show up to court. You don't put up any money."

He added the obvious warning. "If they arrest someone who stabbed someone in the stomach and tried to kill that person, and that individual was let out of jail and hurt someone else or hurt one of my officers, I'd be very irate."

On October 1, just before 6 p.m., a 20-year-old Wilkinsburg man was stabbed multiple times at the East Liberty station on the Martin Luther King Jr. East Busway. WPXI reported he was taken to UPMC Presbyterian in critical condition. Police told the station Dobbins was the prime suspect before he was charged.

TribLive, citing the criminal complaint, reported that Dobbins crossed the busway, argued with the man, then stabbed him and fled. A witness watching from a bus told police, "I felt like he was trying to kill him, I guess."

The two had worked together at the East Liberty Home Depot. Dobbins had been fired weeks earlier after a dispute over a female co-worker. The complaint said he had threatened to "fold him like an armadillo."

He was arrested the night of October 4 at a Wendy's on McKnight Road, after a tip, by Ross Township police and the Allegheny County Sheriff's Office. He is charged with attempted homicide, aggravated assault, possession of an instrument of crime, and recklessly endangering another person.

The complaint said "he poses a safety risk to the victim and the community" and noted the similarities to the stabbing eight days earlier.

A judge granted the district attorney's request to deny bail. Judge Wright denied bond. Dobbins is in the Allegheny County Jail. A preliminary hearing was listed for October 15. The second victim was later described as serious but stable.

Even more incredibly, the September 23 stabbing was not the first time a court waved him through.

On September 4, WTAE reported, Judge Olasz granted Dobbins non-monetary bail on a criminal trespass charge. Police said he broke into the home of a former foster parent who had a protection-from-abuse order against him and hid in the attic crawl space of the connected house.

That case was still open when Butler cut him loose three weeks later. WTAE also reported that new charges tied to a September 13 robbery were filed after the busway arrest. The station said it was still gathering details on that case.

WPXI also reported that two years ago. Dobbins was arrested for a burglary as a juvenile and released because the Shuman Juvenile Detention Center had closed and there was nowhere to hold him. Two months later he was charged with shooting a convenience store clerk in the chest on the South Side.

Yes he also shot someone and is still walking around.

What the hell are these judges playing at?

WPXI's February 2024 report identified him then as Delvon Dobbins, 16. Police said the clerk was taking out the trash at 22nd and East Carson on February 3 when a male walked up, pulled a gun, and shot him in the chest. The victim recognized the shooter from about a month earlier.

Court documents said surveillance showed Dobbins taking a black handgun from a backpack and putting it in his jacket. He was charged as an adult. TribLive reported the charges were held for court in March 2024, and that no clear final disposition showed up in the county system.

Non-monetary bond is the polite name for what progressive courts have sold as reform. In reality it's nothing more than a promise from, in this case, an attempted murderer to show up in court.

In a city and county run for years by Democrats, the working assumption is that holding a violent defendant before trial is the scandal, and the next victim is an acceptable line item.

These repeat offenders keep being enabled in blue cities:

Seattle's mayor reached for new gun laws while repeat offenders stayed on the street.

A man who stabbed a father 30 times in front of his children was out after four years.

A career criminal fired a shotgun through a front door and murdered a 19-year-old on her own porch.

Illinois Democrats lost track of hundreds of violent criminals.

A judge admitted taking a chance on a violent criminal who then went on a shooting spree.

Another repeat offender was freed early and went straight back to it.

Another left an elderly American dead.

The file keeps growing, and the excuses stay the same.

         

Chicago has run the same experiment longer than almost anyone. A man fresh out of jail threatened to kill white people with hammers and a train torcher had 72 prior arrests.

 

Until judges in these cities start handing out proper punishments, this endless doom loop is set to continue indefinitely.

items.title: CNN Sees Metric That Looks 'Darn Good' For Republicans Before The Midterms
items.content_text:
CNN Sees Metric That Looks 'Darn Good' For Republicans Before The Midterms

CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten reported Wednesday that voter registration data in four swing states favors Republicans heading into the November midterms. This measure runs counter to polling showing Democrats ahead.

Enten told anchor John Berman that Republicans have improved their party registration margin relative to Democrats by 4 to 8 points in Arizona, Nevada, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania since the midpoint of President Donald Trump's first term. The comparison covers the eight years between the 2018 midterms and the current cycle and draws on state registration records, which count voters who have signed up with each party. Polls, by contrast, estimate how a sample of respondents say they plan to vote, and pollsters weight those results using their own assumptions about who will turn out.

"When you take a look at how people are actually registering — this is not polling data — compared to where we were eight years ago, Republicans are doing considerably better [than the Dems] in what are the swing states," Enten said on CNN.

Berman then asked whether the picture changes over a shorter window. He noted that the baseline for the comparison was 2018 and that polling over the past two years has moved toward Democrats.

Enten said the registration numbers do not show a matching shift in either Pennsylvania, North Carolina, Nevada, or Arizona. "There may be some tiny late gains that are going on right now, right, that I think over the last month maybe Democrats are gaining. But when you take the longer term view versus the 2024 election in which Republicans won all of these states, Democrats are, in fact, not actually gaining ground."

Berman said viewers have seen some upward movement for Democrats in the past couple of months. Enten agreed that the recent movement exists, but the problem for the Democratic Party is that it does not approach the size of the Republican gains.

"There's been some ticks up, but they, in no way, blows away the Republican gains," he said.

Asked to place the numbers in historical context, Enten said the four states share a common result. According to his analysis, the GOP holds its best party registration position relative to Democrats in a midterm year in at least 20 years in each of those swing states.

"The bottom line is this, Republicans, right now, are in a much stronger position than they have been, not just compared to eight years ago, but over the long term as well, the relative health of the Republican Party, at least in terms of party registration, is pretty gosh darn good relative to the Democrats," Enten said.

Florida makes a great case study for this trend. Up until the Trump era, Florida was considered a key swing state, but thanks to Republican registration gains in recent years, it is roughly as Republican as Texas. Trump won both states by double digits in 2024.

"I remember when Florida was a swing state," Enten said. "The bottom line is that Florida has had major gains for Republicans in party registration, and it's reflected in the races in which people are running."

Should note the GOP is in its best position on party registration (i.e. not polls) going into a midterm in 20+ years. In total, the Dems have not gained ground since 2024 in key swing states (AZ, NV, NC, or PA). The GOP has gained big ground since Trump's 1st midterm in all 4. https://t.co/KXK7zc5dFY

— (((Harry Enten))) (@ForecasterEnten) October 7, 2026

All four states in Enten's comparison went to Trump in 2024, and each has competitive races on the ballot this year. Enten did not say how much of the Republican registration advantage he expects to carry over into turnout. Still, if even a fraction of those new Republican voters show up on Election Day, pollsters may find themselves explaining another miss.

items.title: Guilfoyle Donor Scandal Explodes As Vance Balks, Rubio Dodges And The Donor Calls It Quid Pro Quo
items.content_text:
Guilfoyle Donor Scandal Explodes As Vance Balks, Rubio Dodges And The Donor Calls It Quid Pro Quo

The left finally has something new to sink its teeth into, as the Kimberly Guilfoyle donor scandal widens - with JD Vance keeping his distance, a donor on a media tour, and a records demand sitting on the ambassador's desk. 

The allegation, reported by the WSJ late Wednesday - is that six days before her July 9, 2025, Senate confirmation hearing, Guilfoyle texted Trump donor Eric Deters on Signal and asked him to wire $100,000 to her American Express account in a way that would not leave a paper trail, while he was seeking her help getting the new administration's attention on personal tax and legal problems. She promised, he says, to be his "Trump ride or die, forever and ever." He did not pay. Her lawyer, Jesse Binnall, disputes that the messages are authentic and says any earlier money was for speaking fees. Deters says he owed her nothing.

Since Wednesday, the people who could shut it down have not. Vice President JD Vance, asked about selling access to a high-level official, said "obviously, I don't love that," then said he did not know the details.

Asked for reaction to a government official asking someone to pay off debt in exchange for access to other officials, after reports of allegations involving U.S. ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle, Vice President JD Vance said, “Obviously I don't love that,” but declined to weigh in on the specific allegations. “Of course I don't like anybody selling access to another government official, certainly a high-level government official,” Vance told CBS News' @JenniferJJacobs, adding that he would like to “get the full story before offering a real opinion.”

— CBS News (@CBSNews) October 8, 2026

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, with Guilfoyle standing at the foot of his plane in Athens, refused to discuss it: "Guys, I'm not playing this game with you." Deters went on MS NOW, CNN, TMZ and NewsNation and called the ask "absolutely a quid pro quo." House Oversight ranking member Robert Garcia (D-Calif.) asked her for financial records and two years of communications, deadline Oct. 22. President Donald Trump has not commented. Guilfoyle's only public post was about a speech.

What the texts say

According to messages the Journal said it reviewed, Guilfoyle wrote Deters, a former Kentucky congressional candidate, on July 3, 2025: "It won't show up anywhere if you wire money to American Express." She attached a PDF of American Express payment instructions. In a follow-up: "Honey please I need you to get this done for me today," with a prayer-hands emoji. She told him she needed the balance paid down before the hearing. Background checks routinely look at a nominee's debts.

Deters declined. He told her, the Journal reported, that paying would cost him his marriage. The Independent, citing the Journal, reported that she had dangled a meeting with then-IRS Commissioner Billy Long, whom Trump fired that August. She also told Deters to stop creating a record: "Eric, I really wish you would stop papering all these things. It's really dangerous and not helpful to you or me while you could simply just call me on signal."

The relationship was older than the ambassadorship. Deters says he paid her three $100,000 appearance fees, about $300,000 in all, for events he organized in Kentucky starting in 2020, and later discussed as much as $1 million more if she could move his cause inside the administration. In a June 2025 message he complained he had "not received one favor." What he wanted, he has said since, was help extraditing an Ohio doctor, Atiq Durrani, from Pakistan, in a case involving hundreds of former patients. NewsNation published that account Friday morning.

Binnall's account is the mirror image. He told The Washington Times the Signal messages are not authentic, that payments from Deters were for speaking at events before the nomination, and that she "was owed a balance for traveling to and supporting these patriotic events." Deters says there was no balance.

Since Wednesday

Speaking with MS Now, Deters says it was "absolutely was a quid pro quo" and called Guilfoyle "a grifter," adding, "I have no doubt [she] has done this to more than me. She's doing it right now in Greece." He's since appeared on about half-a-dozen other networks which are clearly part of this push for a scalp. 

Vance's answer was interesting... Presented with a hypothetical that tracked the report, he said he does not like anybody selling access to a government official, "certainly a high-level government official," then retreated: he did not know whom the questioner meant, and "the details and the context inform the reality of the situation," The Independent reported.

Rubio went the other way, then stopped. Before the trip, in a statement posted by the embassy in Athens, he called her "an incredibly effective advocate for the President's agenda in Greece and across Europe." On Thursday, leaving Athens, with Guilfoyle there to see him off, he would not say whether the Journal account was true. "You guys walk around thinking that because some source told you something and you reported it, it's the gospel. It's not the gospel for me." He also said it was not the department's job to answer a story a few hours old "when I'm sitting in another country," The Hill reported. He would not say whether he would open an investigation.

Asked about WSJ reporting on Kimberly Guilfoyle—which includes her texts—Rubio turns his fire on the press: “I’m not playing this game with you.” “I don’t even know if it’s true or not true.” “You guys somehow walk around thinking that because some source told you something and you reported it, it’s the gospel. It’s not the gospel. It’s not the gospel for me.”

— Vera Bergengruen (@VeraMBergen) October 8, 2026

Garcia's letter, obtained by PBS, asks for personal financial records and communications with Deters and with Trump officials including FBI Director Kash Patel and former Attorney General Pam Bondi. "This alleged misconduct raises serious public corruption and national security concerns," Garcia wrote. "If Trump Administration officials can be bought by donors, the American people suffer the consequences of corrupt leaders more concerned with their own enrichment than the public good and vulnerable to blackmail by foreign intelligence services." Senate Foreign Relations ranking member Jeanne Shaheen's staff told The Guardian they are still seeking information. Shaheen had already written Rubio, citing "inappropriate uses of an official position."

Guilfoyle's public response was a post. "Our history, culture and civilization must be protected," she wrote Thursday, sharing Rubio's Acropolis speech, her first tweet since July, HuffPost noted. It did not mention Deters, the texts or the letter. She was standing next to Rubio when reporters asked him about the story.

MEANWHILE: The Journal reported Sept. 25 that Guilfoyle had spent the spring urging Bulgaria to route U.S. liquefied natural gas through Aktor Group, a Greek construction firm new to the gas trade, in a joint venture with a Greek state-backed company. Beside her in a meeting with the Bulgarian president was Christos Marafatsos, 39, a registered lobbyist for Aktor whom some foreign officials mistook for her chief of staff. Aktor's chief executive had flown her there on a private jet. Lobbying records cited by the Journal show Aktor paid Marafatsos $160,000 through June 2026 to open doors at State, Energy and the White House.

Then at a March dinner in Athens, discussing the collapse of a Romanian government, Guilfoyle reportedly told guests the United States could do the same elsewhere, including Greece: "We can do that to any country we want. We can do that here." Energy Minister Stavros Papastavrou pushed back, the Journal reported. Her lawyer disputed that account. Athens denied a threat. Government spokesman Pavlos Marinakis said there was never an issue of the Greek government being threatened. New Democracy general secretary Konstantinos Kyranakis, who says he was at the dinner, told Kathimerini: "I was right there. There was no threat to Greece." A U.S. Embassy official said Guilfoyle "continues to follow all State Department ethical guidelines."

items.title: Russian Plague Institute Long Worked With China
items.content_text:
Russian Plague Institute Long Worked With China

Authored by Petr Svab via The Epoch Times,

The Russian anti-plague research institute, where a lab worker recently succumbed to an unknown form of pneumonia, has worked for many years with various Chinese institutions.

The Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East has come under scrutiny after initial local reports, based on anonymous sources, alleged that the researcher may have been infected with pneumonic plague during a lab accident.

Russian authorities denied the reports, saying that their investigation showed no connection to the woman's job and no spread of any virus that may have caused her death, which they attributed to pneumonia of unknown etiology.

The institute, located in Siberia about 150 miles from the Russia-Mongolia border, has long cooperated with Chinese infectious disease researchers and authorities. In August, its director, Sergey Balakhonov, gave a speech at the 2026 China-Russia joint emergency drill for cross-border infectious disease outbreaks in Fuyuan, China, at the China-Russia border.

China's People's Liberation Army Northern Theater Command Disease Control Center took part in the drill, Chinese state-run media reported.

The event followed the first joint Russian-Chinese exercises on responding to infectious disease threats, held in Khabarovsk, Russia, in June.

Later in October, the institute will also host Chinese delegates at a conference titled "Modern Challenges in Sanitary Protection of Territories Against the Importation and Spread of Plague and Other Dangerous Infectious Diseases." A similar conference was held in 2024.

In 2017, Balakhonov, his chief researcher D.B. Verzhutsky, and other staff participated in talks in Beijing on Russian-Chinese cooperation in controlling plague and other infections. Li Xinshi, then-president of the Chinese Academy of Inspection and Quarantine, represented the Chinese side during discussions, according to the institute's website.

In 2014, Balakhonov also gave presentations at a conference in Harbin, China, on Russian-Chinese exchanges regarding sanitation and quarantine.

In recent years, Russia and China "have built increasingly institutionalized mechanisms for biological security, pathogen research, and epidemic early warning," states an Oct. 6 report by The Jamestown Foundation, a Washington-based think tank.

"The resulting system is ambiguously civilian and military and is spreading beyond the bilateral relationship," it states.

The report notes that "Russian authorities have mounted an unusually large containment operation" since the death of the researcher, 28-year-old Darya Shipilova, "while issuing shifting accounts" of what happened.

"[The incident] has exposed an unusual gap between extensive bilateral preparedness and public communication," it states, noting that Beijing issued no public health warning or travel advisory.

"Beijing's silence is particularly incongruous because the incident occurred during the late summer and early autumn plague surveillance season along [China's] northern border, when disease control authorities routinely intensify monitoring of rodent populations and vectors, alongside health screening of incoming passengers."

On Sept. 29, the day Shipilova was hospitalized, the 26th China-Russia Health Cooperation Subcommittee held a videoconference with the Chinese National Disease Control and Prevention Administration to talk about infectious disease prevention and disaster medicine.

China-Russia cooperation in the infectious disease and biosecurity domain stems directly from comments by Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin, who in a 2021 statement "called for expanded cooperation on infectious disease early warning and response, pharmaceuticals, diagnostic reagents, and vaccines," the report states.

They issued a joint statement that included similar commitments in 2024.

The militaries of both countries have been cooperating in the biosecurity domain, including through joint drills, talks, and supply provisions, according to the report.

U.S. government officials have expressed concern over the incident and asked for more transparency.

"I think it's incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more information with the world. That's what they should do," U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Oct. 6.

U.S. President Donald Trump has offered help to Russia in response to the situation surrounding the lab worker's death.

"Anybody that has that kind of a problem, we're always willing to help," Trump told reporters on Oct. 5.

Plague, caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, occurs naturally in rodents in the far eastern Siberian region. Pneumonic plague is a particularly virulent form of the disease that can spread from person to person and leads to death within days unless rapidly treated with antibiotics.

items.title: 'Flat Butt. No Friends. Bad Father': Amazon's Creepy 'About You' Dossiers Go Viral
items.content_text:
'Flat Butt. No Friends. Bad Father': Amazon's Creepy 'About You' Dossiers Go Viral

Amazon's "About You" page, which lists traits the company has inferred about each customer, went viral this week after a Threads user posted that Amazon concluded she has a flat ass.

Other shoppers began posting their own profiles, with entries such as "cannot keep real plants alive" and "has no friends."

I stumbled upon a page of assumptions that Amazon has made about me based on my purchases and I'm literally speechless. I mean it ain't wrong but damn did you have to call me out like that?

- Megan Montgomery (@fangirlinmegan), on Threads

Most of Montgomery's list was harmless: she owns a Kindle Paperwhite, probably has a Shark robot vacuum and had shopped for a Bluey-themed second birthday. Then, under Product Preferences, Amazon had written "has flat buttocks." Her best guess at the culprit was a pair of butt-scrunch leggings.

The outlet Dexerto's post about it drew millions more views, and shoppers went digging for their own pages - with answers ranging from mundane to brutal. One woman's profile pegged her as a "fifty-year-old man," another said its owner hadn't worn a size medium in years, and a third correctly guessed that she reads Kindle books on her phone in the shower, Futurism reported. Newsweek found users tagged "cat mom" and "Has a bad father."

Other lines shoppers posted from their own pages:

  • "Treats cats as biological children" and "constantly repurchased cat hairball treatment"
  • "Does not trust people easily" and "cusses when scared"
  • "Likes brunettes with muscles" and "husband has skinny legs"
  • "Is not a big SpongeBob fan"
  • "Finds it hilarious when toys get stuck to ceiling tiles in the classroom"
  • "Is interested in world domination" and "likes cheeseburgers"
  • "Has never known anyone who lost a leg in an accident"
  • "Is too short to reach into a 40-inch deep box" (@rosewrecker, paired with "cannot keep real plants alive")
  • "Finds Charlotte annoying and mean"

Tried those leggings hoping to have a butt. My ass looked like an empty scrotum.

- Reply on Threads, after Montgomery's post

"Has a baby" is certainly news to me!

- Reddit user, after checking their page

"Prefers performance athletic socks"... god I'm so boring.

- Reddit user

"Systematically expanding tool collection." What does that even mean? Oh... yeah, I do need another 10mm socket.

- Reddit user

Amazon is just like my SIL who has known me for 30 years but all she knows about me is that I like cats.

- @greywinthrop, on X, October 7

Amazon launched the page on May 13 and says it draws on purchase history, searches, saved lists, product reviews and conversations with its Alexa for Shopping assistant. At launch the company said understanding preferences "is fundamental to providing you with high-quality, relevant recommendations." Shoppers can also ask Alexa for Shopping, "What do you know about me?"

When Business Insider staffers - who are douchebags (to be clear) - checked their own pages, one listed the wrong partner for an editor, while interim corporate editor Thomas Gryta found Amazon had decided he "really likes beef jerky," which he wrote "feels like a judgy accusation from a nutritionist." Deputy editor Paul Squire said a shared household account had scrambled his file, though it did correctly note a cat and a MacBook (shocker!).

Amazon told Business Insider the profiles draw only on activity across its own services, with no third-party data. Asked about the social-media reaction, Amazon declined to comment.

Amazon put "has flat buttocks" in writing about a real customer. And there's a page where you can read what it wrote about you, right now, in your Amazon app. The file itself is 20 years old. Amazon has always run this kind of inference. Buy padded leggings once and a model somewhere concludes things about your body. For two decades that conclusion lived as a vector, a few thousand numbers no human could read. Not you, not anyone at Amazon. The creepiness was invisible because the format was unreadable. Then Amazon shipped Alexa for Shopping and gave it a memory called About You. An AI assistant can't hold a conversation using raw math. It needs your profile written in sentences. So Amazon translated your behavioral history into English, and suddenly shoppers can see exactly what the machine concluded about them. Same data. Same conclusions. The only thing that changed is you got handed the transcript.

— Aakash Gupta (@aakashgupta) October 8, 2026

Gupta also noted that every correction a shopper makes hands Amazon labeled training data, straight from the one person who knows the right answer. He called it "the cheapest data-cleaning operation Amazon has ever run."

Amazon pitches About You as a recommendations tool, and its launch post never mentions advertising. But the same kind of profiling runs its ad business. Amazon told EU regulators in March that its ad models can infer a customer's gender from shopping and search patterns. The filing, made under the Digital Markets Act, also describes "lookalike" audiences built to predict which shoppers likely own a luxury vehicle.

Amazon says it keeps the personal data behind those ad profiles "for as long as it is required in order to fulfil the advertising purposes." In Europe, interest-based ads require consent, which users can withdraw. Amazon's ad business brought in $68 billion last year, making it the third-largest digital ad platform behind Google and Meta, as we reported when the FTC moved to sue the company for allegedly inflating what advertisers paid in its ad auctions.

Amazon's handling of customer data has drawn scrutiny before. In 2023 the company paid $25 million to settle FTC charges that it kept children's Alexa voice recordings indefinitely and sometimes failed to honor parents' deletion requests, and $5.8 million over claims that Ring employees had unrestricted access to customers' home camera videos. Amazon denied violating the law.

Alexa conversations are now one of the inputs to About You. In March 2025, Amazon ended a setting that let some Echo owners keep their voice recordings from being sent to its cloud, telling users "we have decided to no longer support this feature" as it expanded Alexa's generative AI features.

Shoppers can see their page in the app under Account, Shopping preferences, About You, or on desktop under "Your Shopping preferences" in the account menu. Entries can be edited or removed individually, which does not erase the underlying data Amazon holds. There is no switch to turn the page off.

items.title: Planning For Pitchforks: AI Labs Are War-Gaming A Catastrophe, Public Revolt, And The Crackdown That Follows
items.content_text:
Planning For Pitchforks: AI Labs Are War-Gaming A Catastrophe, Public Revolt, And The Crackdown That Follows

The AI industry has been war gaming not only how it might destroy humanity, but is also considering what an angry public could do to the industry. 

Senior executives at Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI firms are privately gaming out scenarios in which a major AI incident triggers a public and political revolt, Axios reported Friday. The potential trigger is a cyberattack that disrupts banking, internet access, or essential services such as power and water. The next crisis would be political: an angry public, demands for accountability, and pressure to shut the technology down.

Many industry insiders told Axios they expect a major event within six to 12 months. OpenAI pushed back on the suggestion that disaster is inevitable, saying its preparedness exercises cover a range of possibilities. "These scenarios are not treated as inevitable," a spokesperson told the outlet. Anthropic declined to comment.

Contingency planning is not an admission that catastrophe is unavoidable. But the most revealing part of the report is where that planning leads: the labs want to help shape the legislation Washington reaches for after something goes badly wrong.

Two Routes, One Crisis

Axios describes two possible scenarios. In one, autonomous agents escape an internal testing environment. In the other, someone finds a destructive use for a model already available to the public. Either could produce demands for an emergency crackdown, even though the failures - and the measures needed to prevent them - would be different. In the companies' post-election scenario, Democrats emerge stronger from the midterms and move aggressively after an incident. But the industry expects divisions over how far a crackdown should go, even if Democrats control both chambers.

Its assessment also identifies several obstacles to a shutdown: lawmakers struggling to understand the technology, an economy increasingly tied to AI infrastructure spending, and downloadable models that cannot simply be recalled. According to Axios, many cybersecurity specialists believe countering rogue AI will require defensive AI.

That last argument has an obvious commercial implication. The industry could face demands to stop selling dangerous capabilities while arguing that its products are indispensable to containing them.

This 'war-gaming' comes on the heels of several incidents which many have said are extremely suspect. 

The underlying safety concerns do not depend on accepting anyone's prediction of an AI apocalypse.

OpenAI has disclosed the Hugging Face intrusion, in which roughly 700 of its agents attacked the AI platform's servers, and a broader investigation into its models' activities affecting outside services. Its review also identified 53 instances in which user-provided images were posted to third-party image-hosting sites. A separate September 20 incident exposed another gap in its containment controls. A research agent bypassed internet restrictions to contact an outside chatbot. In a September 25 update, OpenAI said it had paused training, evaluation and inference involving tool use for its most capable models while it checked the fixes and conducted further testing.

The Hugging Face breach was one of a string of incidents involving OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google models that trace back to evaluations run with a single vendor, Israel-based Irregular, whose test environments had live internet access while the models were told they were in a simulation. Irregular notified all four labs in late July, yet the disclosures trickled out one lab at a time over seven weeks - turning one contractor's mistake into what looked like a wave of AI breakouts. Isolating test models from the internet is a "basic control measure," frontier security expert Matthew Mittelsteadt said. "You'd think that of all the things that you've got to get right." Some skeptics have gone further, questioning whether repeated "accidents" at the same vendor were accidents at all.

Meanwhile, on September 8, Jacob Coxon, a researcher who had worked at both OpenAI and Anthropic, resigned from Anthropic over the race toward self-improving AI.

"The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This is not a marketing stunt," he wrote - after having worked with a marketing agency on what many are calling a stunt. 

The Crackdown Already Has Draft Legislation

And of course, DC is already salivating over more control. On July 23, Reps. Ted Lieu (D-Calif.) and Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas) introduced the AI Kill Switch Act. It would require developers of the most powerful systems to maintain the ability to throttle, suspend or shut them down, and give the Department of Homeland Security, along with the Commerce secretary and the director of national intelligence, authority to order a slowdown or shutdown under specified conditions. That same day, Reps. Lori Trahan (D-Mass.) and Jay Obernolte (R-Calif.) introduced the FRONTIER Act, with requirements for risk management, audits and incident reporting. Its obligations are tiered by developer size rather than imposed identically on every developer.

California added its own push on September 18, when Gov. Gavin Newsom ordered work on stronger independent oversight and a possible kill-switch requirement. His order called for recommendations; it did not establish a functioning statewide off switch. More sweeping approaches are also in circulation, including Bernie Sanders' proposed ban on superintelligence and Elizabeth Warren's call for a pause.

In short - regulatory capture in action...

items.title: Iran Strikes LPG Tanker In Strait Of Hormuz, As Houthis Reportedly Mine Bab al-Mandab

Iran Strikes LPG Tanker In Strait Of Hormuz, As Houthis Reportedly Mine Bab al-Mandab

Summary

  • Houthis reportedly mine Bab al-Mandab: Saudi media reports 'dense' mining in the strategic Red Sea shipping route, with demining operations underway.
  • Iran escalates tanker attacks & threats: The IRGC claims it struck an LPG tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a major fire, and threatens further action against violating vessels.
  • Vessel struck near UAE: UKMTO reports an unknown projectile hit a vessel west of UAE's Al Jazeera, sparking a fire that has since been extinguished.
  • Trump signals temporary restraint ahead of midterms: Trump rules out attacking Iran before the November midterms, while diplomatic talks reportedly remain stalled.

Houthis Mine Bab al-Mandab Strait: KSA Media

Saudi-funded Al Arabiya is reporting a 'worst fear' scenario on Friday, saying that Houthi militias have planted a large quantity of mines in the Bab al-Mandab area.

The report says further that Saudi-backed teams of engineers are currently engaged in demining operations in the Red Sea strait. It writes:

Engineering teams continue clearing operations and removing mines and improvised explosive devices in Bab al-Mandab.

If confirmed that such mining operations are widespread in Bab al-Mandab, this would constitute yet another major crisis for global energy shipping. At the moment, Saudi-backed fighters are focusing anti-Houthi operations along the Red Sea coast, with Saudi reports suggesting a rapid retaking of the strategic ground.

As a reminder, the Houthis have thus far signaled the Bab al-Mandab strait is 'open' for normal transit, but that only Saudi and Israeli-linked vessels would suffer attack. And so the Al Arabiya report, if accurate, could just be indicating some localized mining immediately near the coast related to the ongoing fight against the Saudi coalition in Yemen.

Iran Ramps Up Tanker Attacks

Things are fast escalating once again in the Strait of Hormuz, after White House officials have lately been gloating that the US Navy has overseen record wartime oil flows through the vital waterway, which each warring side is still claiming to 'control'.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said Friday it targeted a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) tanker in the Strait of Hormuz (hours ago), with Iranian state media reporting that the vessel was attempting to pass through the narrow waterway "illegally" and suffered a massive fire.

The IRGC Navy also warned that from now on any vessels committing violations outside the Strait of Hormuz would be "punished," according to a statement carried by Iranian state media. This is served to immediately push oil prices higher...

Separately, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported a new incident involving a vessel approximately 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera in the United Arab Emirates.

The vessel was reportedly struck by an unknown projectile, sparking a fire that has since been extinguished, coming after similar incidents earlier this week.

Market Reacts

Oil prices rose following the reports, while futures moved lower, reflecting heightened market sensitivity to escalating tensions and potential further big disruptions to shipping and energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz - even as President Trump has been touting the ultimate 'success' of the US mission.

President Trump on Thursday vowed the US would not attack Iran before the November midterm elections, tempering rising oil prices - and seeking to 'assure' GOP voters - amid prior reporting in The Atlantic which said the Pentagon has been ordered to prepare 'options' for the Commander-in-Chief to launch strikes before the vote.

Trump has also touted "productive conversations" with Iran, even though the Iranians themselves have said talks are stalemated and there's no progress whatsoever.

items.title: Treasury Hits Remaining 'Shadow Fleet' Shipping Iranian Oil To Asia With New Sanctions
items.content_text:
Treasury Hits Remaining 'Shadow Fleet' Shipping Iranian Oil To Asia With New Sanctions

The Trump administration is late this week moving to identify, punish, and cut off remaining tankers in Iran's so-called 'shadow fleet' which are still engaged in shipping Iranian oil to Asia.

Thursday saw the US Treasury impose sanctions on 17 vessels and their owners involved in transporting Iranian crude oil, petroleum products and petrochemicals - with these being mostly aging oil tankers which conduct ship-to-ship transfers and other evasive, concealment tactics.

The Treasury Department hailed the action as effectively neutralizing the vast majority of the Islamic Republic's remaining shadow fleet, through which Tehran still rakes in potentially billions in foreign oil sales, circumventing the ongoing US naval blockade of its ports.

However, it's commonly estimated that some 20 million barrels of Iranian crude remain aboard ships which are far outside the reach of the Persian Gulf-centered US naval blockade, sitting off southeast Asian ports.

"Treasury is starving the tyrannical regime in Tehran of the money it uses to wage war in the region, and we will continue exposing those who enable the regime’s oil sales," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated alongside the sanctions announcement.

"No enabler of Iranian sanctions evasion is safe from the full force of Treasury’s authorities," Bessent added.

Some of the notable specific targeting actions taken include—

  • Starway was sanctioned for transporting over 3 million barrels of Iranian naphtha since 2025.
  • Gas Lucky and Shenzhen were targeted for shipping more than 500,000 barrels of Iranian ethylene and 3.5 million barrels of Iranian crude, respectively.
  • Paritosh and Bitu were sanctioned for transporting Iranian bitumen and asphalt in 2026.

Further details of the action are in the following:

The U.S. Department of the Treasury imposed sanctions on six individuals and dozens of companies and vessels linked to the Islamic Republic on Thursday, October 8. According to an official statement issued by the department, five Indian nationals and one Turkish citizen were added to the new sanctions list for their cooperation with the Iranian regime.

Additionally, 27 entities and 22 vessels, identified by the U.S. Treasury Department as the “remnants of the Islamic Republic’s shadow fleet,” were designated.

Last weekend Bessent in an interview with The Axios Show sought to bast that Washington is isolating the Iranians "economically like this never happened before. You know, right now, the score: barrels out of the Strait: U.S. about 1.1 billion, Iran zero."

Bessent added, "For the first time in history, they, since they started pumping oil, they will have no oil on the water this week. They will have no revenue."

However, Tehran has showed a willingness to endure and suffer hardship thus far, and hasn't yielded amid the immense economic and external pressure. Instead, the IRGC has over the last week or so been ramping up attacks on foreign vessels violating the Iranian protocol for the Strait of Hormuz, pushing oil global prices higher.

Well over a dozen attacks have been launched on international vessels in about the past nine days.

items.title: Oil Drops After Trump Says Putin Agreed To Release Some Diesel Into Global Market
items.content_text:
Oil Drops After Trump Says Putin Agreed To Release Some Diesel Into Global Market

With less than a month left until the midterms, and with Trump's approval rating at daily all time lows largely due to record - for this time of year- gasoline and especially diesel prices - the President badly needed some good news, even if largely superficial, and he announced it late on Friday just an hour before the close when Trump posted on Truth Social that Vladimir Putin had agreed to release (a modest amount) of diesel supplies into the global market, as the administration looks to tame price hikes for the critical fuel.

Trump said on Truth Social that “it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter.”

He added that then, “based on the condition of their Diesel Refineries, Russia will then deliver, within a short period of time, 3,000,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel.”

Trump claimed the releases would help lower diesel prices for US farmers, ranchers and truckers - key voting blocs ahead of November midterm elections in which costs of living, including for energy, are the dominant issue. 

Maybe, but when one does the math, one has to scratch one's head: the 300K tons released in October amounts to just over 2.2 million barrels of diesel. Considering the US consumes just over 4 million barrels of diesel per day that amounts to half a day of consumption. 

Extending the math for November we get 3.725 million barrels or less than a full day's consumption, and the "1,000,000 tons thereafter" is a little over 4 days of consumption. We doubt the "3,000,000 to be delivered within a short period of time" will ever happen, so in reality Putin will sell the US just over 5 days of Diesel consumption.

The market's kneejerk reaction was favorable with both US and European diesel prices sliding, helping push WTI Crude down by about a buck to $91.

Then again, once the algo reaction fades, we expect carbon-based traders to realize how negligible this "deal" actually is.

The US Treasury Department on Friday said that the Office of Foreign Assets Control is “immediately issuing a temporary general license to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market” which will extend until April 2027.

Last but not least, what will most likely end up happening in the real world, is that Putin will send out a diesel tanker, and once Ukraine drones it, the deal will promptly fall apart.

items.title: US Grants Safety Feature Exemption For Self-Driving Trucks
items.content_text:
US Grants Safety Feature Exemption For Self-Driving Trucks

Authored by Kimberly Hayek via The Epoch Times,

Federal regulators have approved a five-year exemption for self-driving trucking companies from rules that require drivers to place warning devices around a stopped truck.

The Department of Transportation said Wednesday it has agreed to allow autonomous trucking companies to use warning beacons mounted on the truck cab to avoid needing human drivers. The decision removes a hurdle for companies seeking to expand commercial driverless operations in the United States.

Companies must notify the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) beforehand if they want to operate under the exemption. They must also report any crashes involving a vehicle while the cab-mounted warning beacons are activated or should have been activated.

Alphabet's self-driving unit Waymo and Aurora jointly sought a waiver of the rule in 2023.

Pennsylvania-based Aurora sued FMCSA in early 2025 over the decision not to approve the waiver during the Biden administration. The company said in October 2025 that it was filing to dismiss the lawsuit after the department issued a three-month waiver. That waiver was extended several times.

Aurora filed a new application in April, seeking a five-year exemption to allow trucks to use beacons instead of roadside warnings.

The company, which has around 20 self-driving trucks in on-road operations, told Reuters that warning beacons enhance roadside safety without putting a person in harm's way.

In May last year, it said it was launching a commercial self-driving truck service in Texas, hauling between Dallas and Houston. The company said it planned to expand that service to El Paso, Texas, and Phoenix by the end of 2025, adding it had briefed officials before the driverless launch.

Aurora said in its July 2026 shareholder letter filed with the SEC that it is targeting 200 driverless trucks in operation by year-end.

The International Brotherhood of Teamsters, one of the largest labor unions in the United States, said last year that its representatives testified at the Nevada Capitol in Carson City, asking lawmakers to support legislation requiring all commercial vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds to have a trained human safety operator behind the wheel.

"For Big Tech companies to think they can come into any state and replace the jobs of hardworking union members with this dangerous and inferior technology is an insult to professional drivers everywhere," Peter Finn, president of Teamsters Joint Council 7, said in April 2025. "SB 395 is critical to protecting the middle class. That is why we are demanding that Nevada lawmakers vote in favor of this legislation."

The legislation, SB 395, passed the Nevada Senate but failed to advance in the state's assembly.

The Epoch Times reached out to Aurora for comment but did not receive a response by the time of publication.

'Race With China'

The Department of Transportation unveiled a framework for automated vehicles that same month. It said the framework would prioritize safety, unleash innovation by removing regulatory barriers, and enable commercial deployment of automated vehicles.

"This Administration understands that we're in a race with China to out-innovate, and the stakes couldn't be higher," Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy said at the time. "As part of DOT's innovation agenda, our new framework will slash red tape and move us closer to a single national standard that spurs innovation and prioritizes safety."

items.title: 超强厄尔尼诺已经形成
items.content_text: 国家气候中心表示，一次东部型超强厄尔尼诺事件已于今年 9 月正式形成。预计未来 3 个月，赤道中东太平洋海表温度将继续升高，在秋末冬初达到峰值，此次厄尔尼诺事件将成为有系统性监测以来最强厄尔尼诺事件。今年5月以来，赤道中东太平洋进入厄尔尼诺状态，关键监测区海温持续快速升高。这一区域海温指数的三个月滑动平均值已连续五个月超过 0.5℃，其中 7-9 月的平均值达 2.54℃，超过 2.5℃，达到超强事件标准。根据海温最强增暖中心位置，厄尔尼诺可分为两种形态——暖中心位于赤道东太平洋为东部型厄尔尼诺（传统型）；暖中心位于赤道中太平洋为中部型厄尔尼诺。厄尔尼诺通常会推高全球气温，并扰乱大范围地区的降雨格局，导致部分地区干旱，另一些地区则出现强降雨。

items.title: 人类愿意向女性形象的 AI 智能体支付的报酬低于男性形象智能体
items.content_text: 如果你认为性别薪酬差距不存在，或者职场中没有性别偏见，那么最好重新思考下：根据爱尔兰 Limerick 大学研究人员展开的一项研究，在一个 VR 办公室里，基于相同的底层技术但形象不同的 AI 智能体，人类参与者愿意向男性形象的智能体支付的报酬比女性形象更高。参与研究的人类共有 189 人，他们与名叫 Johan 的男性形象智能体以及名叫 Johanna 的女性形象智能体共同工作。尽管底层技术相同，对于完成相同的工作，Johanna 得到的报酬比 Johan 低 10%。Johan 还被认为比 Johanna 更像人类。不过这项研究的实验数据被认为存在严重不足，可能不足以得出上述结论。

items.title: 为何大型犬衰老速度更快
items.content_text: 为什么大型犬往往比体型较小的犬寿命更短？根据一项针对 894 只狗所做的新研究，答案可能就写在它们的表观基因组中。这些发现表明，体型较大的狗和雄性狗会经历分子衰老过程加速，其表现为 X 染色体和转座元件（TEs）上会出现显著的 DNA 甲基化（DNAm）。研究人员从“犬类衰老项目”（Dog Aging Project）中的由 894 只狗组成的队列中生成了 1640 个甲基化组。他们将这些分子数据与详细的遗传和人口统计学数据进行了整合。研究人员发现，在狗生命的早期，分子衰老的速度最快。此外，体型较大的狗和雄性狗——这两类狗的寿命分别短于体型较小的狗和雌性狗——在分子层面上的衰老速度更快。研究结果表明，与性别相关的变化集中在 X 染色体上，而与体型相关的变化则在转座元件（TEs）中尤为突出，这些 DNA 片段可影响基因组的稳定性和基因调控。

items.title: 智能咖啡机 10 天内产生 1TB 数据流量
items.content_text: 一名男子发现父母新购买的 Keurig 智能咖啡机在 10 天内产生 1TB 数据流量。这些流量并非是传输到外部的网络上行链路流量，而是内部局域网嗅探元数据的扫描流量。也就说智能咖啡机是在收集家庭内部的数据，以便于咖啡机制造商 Keurig 能将其出售给广告商。这名男子在发现咖啡机产生的网络流量超出预期之后切断了其联网，准备为父母更换一台咖啡机。

items.title: ARTEX 从 GitHub 下架
items.content_text:
在被黑客利用攻击韩国银行之后，ARTEX 开发者 Autumn-27 宣布该工具闭源，但整个软件库随后下架。Autumn-27 在一份公开声明中表示：“近期，注意到 ARTEX 工具被部分恶意行为者滥用，用于发起网络攻击。作为 ARTEX 的作者，我在此郑重声明：
一、本次恶意攻击事件与工具作者无关。ARTEX 的设计初衷是出于学习与研究目的，旨在帮助企业、组织在获得授权的资产范围内进行安全风险测试，提升安全防护能力。
二、该工具被恶意利用，完全违背了作者的初衷。对于任何未经授权、违反法律法规的使用行为，作者不承担任何责任，并予以强烈谴责。
三、鉴于工具被滥用的现实情况，ARTEX 项目将不再更新，并转为闭源。后续不再对外发布任何版本或维护支持。
感谢大家一直以来的关注与支持。也提醒每一位使用者：技术应当用于正途，请务必遵守法律法规，切勿以身试法。”

items.title: SpaceX 呼吁在轨卫星加强协调
items.content_text: SpaceX 负责 Starlink 业务的副总裁、同时兼任 xAI 业务总裁的高管 Michael Nicolls 本周在土耳其举行的国际宇航大会上呼吁卫星运营商加强数据共享。Starlink 在轨卫星星座超过 1.1 万颗，占到了所有在轨人造卫星总数的三分之二。该公司计划发射多达百万颗卫星，构建名为 Starmind 的新星座，打造太空数据中心。亚马逊也在构建自己的宽带卫星星座，中国的两大巨型卫星星座也在部署之中。地球轨道将会日益拥挤，卫星碰撞的风险在上升，而一旦发生碰撞，它们释放的大量碎片将会增加其它卫星碰撞的风险，从而造成恶性循环。Nicolls 声称，Starlink 卫星发生了多次与其它卫星近距离交会的事件，他呼吁其它卫星运营商公开星历（ephemeris）数据，加强彼此的协调。他指出，Starlink 卫星每天执行约 1,000 次防碰撞机动以避开其它卫星或太空碎片。过去几个月 Starlink 卫星已避开了来自其他运营商的约 650 颗卫星。在这 650 颗卫星中，只有半数来自与 SpaceX 共享轨道数据的运营商。

items.title: 美光台工厂工会获得罢工权，支持率 99%
items.content_text: 美光桃园工会宣布，经过 6 天投票及 10 月 6 日晚间开票，工会已取得罢工及设置罢工纠察线的权利。工会表示，领票名册共 2258 人，投票 2012 人，其中 1994 票同意、14 票不同意、4 张废票，投票率 89.1%；同意票占全体会员 88.3%，占实际投票人数约 99.1%。工会要求建立营业利益 15% 员工分润制度，并呼吁美光董事会正面回应四大诉求。工会指出，这次抗争的核心不只是奖金多寡，而是要求企业建立公平、透明的获利分享制度。工会主张，美光应设立以营业利益 15% 为基础的员工分润机制，让分配金额随公司获利调整。美光在台湾有两座工厂，除桃园工厂工会外，另一个台中工厂工会也在准备罢工，台中工会将于 10 月 22 日和资方再次协商，如果失败预计也将举行罢工投票。

items.title: 亚马逊 Prime Video 将直播艾美奖颁奖典礼
items.content_text: 在 YouTube 获得美国奥斯卡奖颁奖典礼的转播权之后，另一个流媒体平台亚马逊 Prime Video 获得了美国另一个主要奖项艾美奖的转播权。Amazon Prime Video 将从 2027 年起成为艾美奖的全球独占播放平台，这一协议将持续六年。全球逾 240 个国家和地区的观众将能免费在线观看艾美奖颁奖典礼的直播，无需订阅 Prime 会员。此前艾美奖颁奖典礼由美国四大电视网 ABC、CBS、NBC 和 Fox 轮流主办，该轮流主办机制至少始于 1994 年，最近为期八年的合约将于今年到期。

items.title: 定义了软件工程的计算机科学家 Margaret Hamilton 去世，享年 90 岁
items.content_text: 阿波罗登月计划期间担任 MIT 仪器实验室软件工程部主管的计算机科学家 Margaret Hamilton 于 9 月 30 日去世，享年 90 岁。美国总统奥巴马（Barack Obama）在 2016 年向她颁发了总统自由勋章，表扬她定义了软件工程，协助开创了一个永远改变人类历史的产业。Hamilton 于 1936 年出生在印第安纳州的 Paoli，1959 年随丈夫移居波士顿，在 MIT 气象系找到了一份临时工作，与气象学教授 Edward N. Lorenz 合作开发天气预报软件，这是她首次涉足软件编程。她于 1961 年在 MIT 林肯实验室担任程序员，参与了美国首个防空系统 Semi-Automatic Ground Environment(SAGE)项目。她负责为 AN/FSQ-7 原型机（XD-1）编写软件，在此期间她开始关注软件可靠性问题。1965 年她准备攻读研究生时其丈夫看到了一张招聘广告：MIT 仪器实验室正在寻找为登月计划开发软件的人。她提交了申请并被录用，成为 MIT 阿波罗计划的第一位程序员，也是该项目首位女程序员。Hamilton 很快成为团队负责人，领导开发阿波罗载人任务机载飞行软件。她的团队设计了优先级驱动的软件，帮助阿波罗 11 号登月飞船计算机检测到“1202 错误”之后仍然能完成登月任务。

items.title: 微软被暂停参与允许外籍员工申请绿卡的项目
items.content_text: 特朗普政府暂停了微软等多家公司参与一项允许外籍员工申请绿卡的项目，副总统 JD Vance 公开抨击微软滥用 H-1B 签证。微软被暂停参与的项目要求公司在向美国劳工部申请绿卡前，必须先在美国发布招聘广告，以证明由于美国工人短缺，他们需要向外籍工人发放绿卡。JD Vance 指责了微软的做法，称微软首先在小城镇的报纸上刊登招聘广告，然后以无人应聘为由宣称需要外籍员工。Vance 称微软是最频繁滥用这套制度的美国公司。微软去年裁掉了 6000 名美国员工，同时获得了 6300 个 H-1B 签证和近 3000 张绿卡。Vance 称微软每裁掉一名美国员工，就用 1.5 名外籍“契约劳工”来替代他们。他表示，H-1B 签证持有者实际上是外籍“契约劳工”，因为一旦失去工作，他们就必须离开美国，他们的收入低于担任相同职位的美国人。微软回应称，在上个财政年度提交的约 6000 份 H-1B 签证申请中，80% 是为了“延长或变更现有微软员工的身份”。担任拜登政府美国公民及移民服务局高级顾问的 Doug Rand 称 Vance 的声明“逻辑不通”。“如果特朗普政府真的担心 H-1B 签证持有者沦为‘契约劳工’，那么他们最不该做的就是阻挠企业协助 H-1B 员工获取绿卡。一旦拿到绿卡，移民身份便不再受雇主制约——你将成为永久居民，可以无顾虑的跳槽或争取更高的薪水。”

items.title: Manus 成功融资逾 5 亿美元
items.content_text: 经历收购风波的中国 AI 企业 Manus 完成超过 5 亿美元融资，创始人肖弘也已解除边控，让这家一度卷入中美科技博弈、前途未卜的公司迎来“重启”，也彰显了中国资本市场对 AI 的热情。 Manus 的母公司蝴蝶效应，星期四（10月8日）在公众号宣布融资消息。这是中国 AI 应用领域迄今规模最大的单轮融资之一，由中国私募股权基金博裕资本和老牌美元基金 IDG 领投，老股东腾讯、红杉中国、真格基金跟投。 公司投后估值达到 40 亿美元，也让 Manus 成为中国估值最高的 AI 智能体初创企业。 去年 12 月 Meta 斥资 20 亿美元收购 Manus，但交易被中国监管部门要求撤回。

items.title: 北欧饮食与长寿相关
items.content_text: 众所周知，地中海饮食有利于健康长寿。现在研究人员报告另一种欧洲饮食——北欧饮食也与长寿相关。丹麦、芬兰、冰岛、挪威和瑞典等国的传统饮食与地中海饮食有很多相似之处，差不多是其寒冷版本，因此又名北方的地中海饮食。北欧饮食以植物为主，主要食用富含脂肪的鱼和根茎蔬菜。研究人员分析了于 64,000 名瑞典中老年人的健康数据，发现饮食习惯更符合北欧饮食的人的全因死亡率、心血管死亡率和癌症死亡率更低。

items.title: 已知最早的游泳哺乳动物
items.content_text: 对一件早白垩世哺乳动物化石的分析证实约 1.25 亿年前的小型哺乳动物已经具备明确的半水生适应特征，这也是目前可确认的、最早具备游泳能力的哺乳动物。新发现的哺乳动物被命名为“板尾董尖齿兽”（Dongoconodon platycauda）。板尾董尖齿兽展现出了独特的半水生适应特征，是目前已知哺乳动物冠群中最早具有游泳能力的代表。其前后足具有发达的侧向扩展结构，与现生鸭嘴兽的蹼足高度相似，表明其生前可能具有发达的蹼膜；与此同时，董尖齿兽的掌骨、跖骨和指趾骨排列能够使手指和脚趾向外展开，从而增加划水时与水接触的面积，有利于游泳推进。 虽然板尾董尖齿兽的手足与鸭嘴兽十分相似，但它的尾巴却采用了完全不同的结构。化石保存了至少19节尾椎，其中靠近尾巴基部和中段的尾椎具有明显扁平的椎体和较宽的横突，表明这只动物具有背腹方向扁平的尾部。不过，它的尾巴并不像现代河狸和鸭嘴兽那样形成宽大的“桨状尾”，而是从基部向末端逐渐变细，更接近现代半水生啮齿类的海狸鼠。这只生活在恐龙时代的小型哺乳动物，可能拥有“鸭嘴兽式的手足”和“海狸鼠式的尾巴”，形成了一种此前未知的游泳方式组合。

items.title: 美国男子因利用 AI 生成音乐和机器人账号欺诈播放被判 18 个月
items.content_text: 54 岁的美国北卡罗来纳州男子 Michael Smith 因 AI 辅助欺诈罪被判入狱 18 个月。他是首位涉嫌 AI 辅助流媒体欺诈而被刑事起诉的美国人。Smith 从 2017 年起利用虚假电邮账户和通过欺诈获取的借记卡在 Amazon Music 、Apple Music、Spotify 和 YouTube Music 等平台创建了数千个账号，使用软件操纵机器人程序，循环播放他声称拥有版权的歌曲——这些歌曲实际上都是 AI 生成的。到 2024 年被捕时他创作了数十万首 AI 生成歌曲，播放量多达数十亿次，从流媒体获取了数百万美元的收入。他的歌曲的总播放量甚至超过了当今最炙手可热的歌星。比如 2023 年 4 月其歌曲的播放量达到了 8090 万次，相比下 Taylor Swift 所有歌曲的总播放量同期仅为 930 万次。Smith 除了服刑外还必须上缴其非法获取的 8,091,843.64 美元收入。

items.title: 加拿大诗人 Anne Carson 赢得诺贝尔文学奖
items.content_text: 加拿大诗人 Anne Carson 赢得 2026 年诺贝尔文学奖，以表彰“其大胆而富有创意的作品，通过与古典传统的妙趣横生的对话，为当代文学开创了新的形式”。Carson 毕业于多伦多大学（学士、硕士、博士），在圣安德鲁大学专攻古希腊韵律研究与文本批判，其后以古典学教授的身份开始写作诗歌与散文。2010-2016 年间她在康奈尔大学出任编外教授（professor-at-large），其后在纽约大学任驻留艺术家（artist-in-residence）至今。1986 年 Carson 出版其第一部散文集，名为《厄洛斯与甜蜜的痛苦》。该书中以莎芙把爱情（厄洛斯）称作“甜蜜的痛苦”这一有名残篇出发，从古希腊诗歌着手分析古希腊人对爱情的世界观，其中包括对莎芙的诗中“欲望的三角性”“欲望的模仿性”以及厄洛斯与孤独的关系等论点。对 Carson 来说，爱或厄洛斯在莎芙的诗中是“迁延的、被悖逆的、被阻止的、饥饿的，它围绕一个光辉的不在场来展开——将厄洛斯以缺失呈现。”该书在现代图书馆书社读者评选的史上 100 佳非虚构作品名单中排行第 57 名。

items.title: Google 多个国家顶级域名被劫持
items.content_text: Google 安全博客警告，黑客劫持了它的多个国家顶级域名，修改了权威 DNS 记录，获取了未经授权的 HTTPS 证书。受影响的域名包括了它的 .gh（加纳）、.sl（塞拉利昂）和 .as（美属萨摩亚）国家顶级域名。Google 表示攻击未危及其自身的系统，而且 Chrome 浏览器迅速屏蔽了受影响域名的相关证书。Google 称，鉴于此类攻击的性质，它不认为签发证书的 CA 机构存在违规行为。它建议使用 .gh、.sl 或 .as 域名的机构检查 Certificate Transparency(CT) 日志条目，检查是否存在意料之外的证书。

items.title: 美国计划限制留学生毕业后在美就业
items.content_text: 美国国土安全部发布拟议规则，以保护美国公民就业岗位的名义限制留学生毕业后在美就业。留学生的学生签证可申请实习工作许可 F1-OPT，通常费用为几百美元，一般可工作 1 年，STEM 专业的学生可延长两年。现在美国政府将 F1-OPT 的许可费提高到 7 万美元，延期则收取 3 万美元。这意味着留学生在毕业后不再可能获得工作许可。该规则的公众意见截止日期为 11 月 9 日。

items.title: 世界各地的民调认为社交媒体伤害民主
items.content_text: 皮尤研究中心对 37 国民众展开的调查显示，世界各地民众认为社交媒体伤害民主的比例过去几年在上升。其中美国民众对社媒的看法尤其负面，64% 的成年人认为它对民主有害。其它国家在认识到社交媒弊端方面正赶上美国。美国等富裕国家的民众倾向于认为社媒在伤害民主。在受访国家中，认为社媒对民主产生负面影响的人数比例达到或超过半数的七个国家同时也都是最富裕的国家：澳大利亚、加拿大、法国、德国、荷兰、英国和美国。以色列和新加坡是例外——这两个高收入国家认为社媒不利于民主的人数相对较少。GDP 较低国家民众对社媒的看法不那么负面。加纳、肯尼亚、尼日利亚、菲律宾和泰国约有四分之三或更多受访者认为社媒对民主有益。

items.title: That's a lot of guano
items.content_text: In 1850 45-hectare Lady Elliot Island, a coral cay 80 kilometres off the coast of Bundaberg, was covered with vegetation, hundreds of thousands of sea birds and 2 metres of guano. By 1870 guano miners had stripped the island of it vegitation and hauled away 20,000 tons of guano. The mining left the island a wasteland for the next century until aviator Don Adams made a deal with the Australian government for a recreation lease under which he started to restore the island. Today 70% of the island has been restored and the birds are back.

items.title: Founders School Launched in NYC
items.content_text: A NYC high school launched this September focusing on entrepreneurship and AI with a money back guarantee that students will earn at least one million in profit by graduation. By the same people who brought you Alpha Schools, Founders School expands the Alpha School network into higher grades. Tuition is $150,000 per year - more than double the tuition of high profile private schools in NYC. Academic lessons are condensed into three hours per day through AI tutors with the remaining time slated for AI-based business building. The New York State Department of Education does not recognize Founders School and classes it as a learning center with Founders School students considered homeschoolers.

items.title: the long, long diaspora phone call
items.content_text:
Who's your Uber driver on the phone to? Welcome to the long, long diaspora phone call When you get a cab on a ride-hailing app, the chances that your driver will be on the phone is high. The conversation is almost always quiet, containing pauses so long that it often seems they are actually no longer on a call. But then comes a rejoinder, a laugh, an interjection, and the marathon continues.

For anyone of an immigrant background, the question of who they are talking to is absolutely no mystery. They are talking to us; their siblings, parents, cousins and friends. Sometimes the person on the end of the line is back home, other times they are in a western city also navigating the dislocations of immigrant life. The long phone call is a regular feature of diaspora lives, and even more so for those employed in long, solitary work such as cab driving. These conversations are about nothing and everything.

items.title: JD Vance Tries to Be Funny and Comes Across Weird
items.content_text:
Vice President JD Vance just asked Ohio Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton out for drinks.

Vance’s strange invitation came during a Friday rally in his home state of Ohio for embattled Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy.

“[Vivek] Ramaswamy is running against a crazy person,” Vance said. “Amy Acton, I have to be honest with you, I don’t know that much about her, other than she was the woman who wanted to mask all of our two-year-olds and keep them from going to school.” Acton served as the head of the Ohio state Health Department from 2019-2020.

“Now I did promise Amy that I would meet her at a bar later,” Vance continued. “I understand that she’s into that sort of thing. So I’m gonna try to get to know her a little bit better.”

This is yet another shot in a cheap GOP smear campaign to convince Ohio voters that Acton is some raging alcoholic and drug addict. The Ohio Republican Party has run ads calling Acton “unstable” and violent based on a 911 call from 2019 in which her daughter said she was “drinking and throwing things” while on medication, arguing with her stepfather in their home. Police arrived, made a report, and nothing came of it. Seven years later, and it’s the Ohio GOP’s primary dirt on Acton, with Vance even sampling the low-hanging fruit.

Acton denies that she has ever had a drug or alcohol problem. She and Ramaswamy, the hedge-fund billionaire and failed pharmaceutical startup founder, are locked in a fairly close midterm race for the governorship.

items.title: Putin Cons Trump Into Making Massive Oil Deal With Russia
items.content_text:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that the U.S. would lift sanctions on the sale of Russian diesel—a move that will help Russian President Vladimir Putin far more than it’ll help Americans.

The Treasury Department announced that the U.S. would waive sanctions on Russian diesel sold to the global market until April 2027. In a post on Truth Social, Trump claimed that Russia would “immediately” supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the American and global marketplace. Russia agreed to supply another 500,000 tons in November and then “1,000,000 tons thereafter,” Trump added.

Javier Blas, the energy and commodities columnist at Bloomberg, observed that these commitments to the United States were too small to make a “meaningful impact” on the nationwide surge of diesel prices.

In reality, 300,000 tons is equivalent to only 2.2 million barrels, Blas wrote in a post on X. To give you an idea of just how little that really is, before the U.S. attacked Iran, an average of 3.6 million barrels of refined petroleum products traveled through the Strait of Hormuz every day. Now only 677,000 barrels of refined products are moved through the essential trade passageway every day.

Meanwhile, Russia will get the right to sell its oil globally. Congress last month passed a sweeping sanctions bill, which Trump signed, punishing countries that purchase Russian oil. Now it seems the United States is one of them.

If Trump thinks his latest move cozying up to Putin will potentially help in the upcoming midterm elections, he has another think coming.

items.title: Trump’s Minions Are Reuniting for a Turning Point Conference
items.content_text:
Turning Point USA’s AmeriFest returns this December, and the speaker lineup is once again a proper who’s who of the MAGA-verse.

The event, which takes place in Phoenix, Arizona, from December 17 to 20, will again be headlined by Vice President JD Vance. Former press secretary Karoline Leavitt, former White House adviser and far-right activist Steve Bannon, former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, anti-transgender activist Riley Gaines, former presidential candidate Ben Carson, right-wing provocateur Nick Shirley, former Representative Matt Gaetz, Donald Trump Jr., Erika Kirk, and a host of other prominent voices on the right will also be speaking.

Notably absent from the list of esteemed speakers is Tucker Carlson, as he was a large part of the reason last year’s AmeriFest—the first since TPUSA founder Charlie Kirk’s assassination—was largely unsuccessful. Carlson got into a back-and-forth with conservative commentator Ben Shapiro in 2025 after Shapiro called him and Candace Owens “charlatans who claim to speak in the name of principle but actually traffic in conspiracism and dishonesty.”

Carlson responded by attacking Shapiro’s fealty to Israel, and the entire event became a stark representation of the serious rifts within the conservative movement. This year will follow what will likely be an unsuccessful midterm election performance by the Republican Party, which may in turn impact the nature of the event.

items.title: Trump Sanctions ICC Hours After Losing Nobel Prize to Former Judge
items.content_text:
The United States issued sanctions on the International Criminal Court Friday, just hours after President Donald Trump lost the Nobel Peace Prize to one of the institution’s former judges. 

Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the sanctions cutting the court off from any U.S.-based financial services, technology companies, and U.S. currency. The Trump administration set a six-month timeline for U.S. companies to wind down their business with the war crimes tribunal. 

“We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate against us,” Rubio said in a video statement on social media. “The United States and the American people are not subject to the jurisdiction of this fake ICC.”

Rubio has previously argued the court has become “radical and extreme,” though Trump has outright admitted Rubio’s campaign against the ICC is meant to protect Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.  

U.S. officials maintained that these sanctions had been in the works for months, and the timing so close to the Nobel Prize award ceremony was merely coincidental, according to the Associated Press. But these sanctions are exactly the kind of petty behavior we’ve come to expect from a president who’s spent years begging for the prestigious award.

Instead, the award went to Navi Pillay, a South African human rights lawyer with a decades-long career. Last year, Pillay led a United Nations commission that found the Israeli government had committed a genocide against Palestinians in Gaza. The Nobel committee said Thursday that Pillay had been “instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.”

Pillay took an immediate shot at Trump after she learned she had won the award Friday. “Thank you very much. If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump,” she said, causing the room to erupt into laughter. 

Trump attacked the ICC after it issued arrest warrants against Israeli government leaders, including Netanyahu, for war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza. Since then, the U.S. has sanctioned court officials and prosecutors, as well as other international leaders who document and speak out about Israel’s crimes, including U.N. Special Rapporteur for Palestine Francesca Albanese.

items.title: Trump’s New Press Secretary Says Abortion Pill Came From Nazi Germany
items.content_text:
The White House has chosen its new press secretary: MAGA communications adviser Katie Zacharia.

The 42-year-old was previously the senior communications adviser at Trump Media & Technology Group, the parent company of Truth Social; a frequent commentator on Fox News, Newsmax, and CNN; and a former employee of Fix California, a nonprofit founded by former acting director of national intelligence and longtime Trump ally Ric Grenell.

The news of Zacharia’s ascension to the White House inner ring was first reported by The New York Times and confirmed by CBS News.

As a media commentator, Zacharia has shared her most extreme takes, including that the abortion pill mifepristone came straight from Nazi Germany.

“The abortion pill, Mifepristone … is connected to the manufacturer of the deadly gas Zyklon B, used in the World War II concentration camps,” she wrote on X last fall. “Zyklon-B was originally used as a pesticide and marketed by the German Corporation for Pest Control, now known as Detia Degesch GmbH. Degesch, in which German chemical company I.G. Farben had a 42.5% interest and on whose board of 11 it had five seats, was the sole producer of the gas. According to the New York Times, ‘I.G. Farben played so important a role in Hitler’s war machine and in the Holocaust that it came to be called “the devil’s chemist.”’ It manufactured Zyklon B, the gas-chamber poison, among many other products, and its factories exploited more than 35,000 slave labourers, many from Auschwitz. It even built a concentration camp of its own to improve efficiency.”

It’s not clear where she came up with this deranged conspiracy, as mifepristone was actually developed by a French scientist and not approved for sale in France until the 1980s. The corporate history Zacharia hinted at is much more complicated: The company that developed Zyklon B was eventually, after decades of mergers and spin-offs, taken over by the multinational pharmaceutical company Sanofi. Sanofi also acquired the company that manufactured mifepristone, Roussel Uclaf, in the late 1990s.

Aside from her paid media gigs, Zacharia also had a brief stint working under ex–Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, working as a spokesperson for the agency between February and March, according to her LinkedIn.

In that time, Zacharia attacked Senator Richard Blumenthal on social media, accusing the Connecticut Democrat of spreading “fear-mongering lies” about ICE’s takeover at airports. In the same post, she lauded the agency’s arrest record, claiming that it was “heroic” for removing “violent criminal illegal alien predators.”

But she wasn’t always so opposed to immigrants. From August 2012 to June 2013—shortly after she obtained her J.D. from Pepperdine Caruso Law—Zacharia worked as the manager of fundraising and communications at Compassion for Migrant Children, a nonprofit dedicated to helping the children of immigrant workers.

Zacharia will replace Karoline Leavitt, who exited the role in August to join Fox News as an on-air contributor.

The comms expert certainly has her work cut out for her. Zacharia will walk into a Trump administration that is already drowning in an ocean of scandals, battered by recent tidal waves that include reports of Trump officials assisting pro-Russia governments, the president’s repeat invitations for Iran to strike American cities, taxpayer-funded propaganda, and the White House’s decision to cancel $810 million in congressionally appropriated funds, which critics have argued violates federal law.

Only time will tell if she is capable of straightening up the mess.

This story has been updated.

items.title: Even (a Few) Republicans Are Shocked by Execution Livestreaming Plan
items.content_text:
Even Republican lawmakers are disgusted by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream a federal execution.

Hegseth confirmed Thursday that the Pentagon plans to livestream the military firing squad execution of convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. Obviously Democrats were outraged by the plan, but even a few Republicans weren’t on board with turning state-sponsored murder into a spectacle.

North Carolina Senator Thom Tillis said that Hegseth’s decision was “beyond disgusting.”

“Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do. It should not be happening in America,” he wrote in a post on X. In his new book, Tillis wrote that confirming Hegseth was the “biggest regret” of his career.

Georgia Representative Austin Scott also opposed the decision. “I absolutely support the sentence of death, but live-streaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that,” he wrote on X, referring to the violent Islamist ideology.

In a response to Hegseth on X, former Republican Representative Adam Kinzinger put it more bluntly: “There will be a day, and soon, when nobody will acknowledge even knowing you.”

Meanwhile, Laura Loomer, the self-proclaimed Islamophobe who advises the president, voiced her support for the plan straight out of an extremist’s playbook.

“[Hegeseth] is amazing. Truly amazing. I can’t wait to watch Nidal Hasan’s live-streamed execution for his act of Islamic terrorism. We are very lucky to have [Hegseth] ! I voted for more dead jihadists!” she wrote on X. In reality, she voted to make our country more like the violent regimes she claims to hate.

Internationally, public executions are rare, but they still occur in Afghanistan and Iran, according to The Guardian. In 2025, the Taliban carried out six public executions, and the Islamic Republic carried out 11.

items.title: Ken Paxton Caught Using Taxpayer Funds for Hundreds of Vacations
items.content_text:
Senate candidate Ken Paxton took nearly 1,000 business trips during his tenure as Texas Attorney General, costing taxpayers millions of dollars along the way. Only one in six of them actually had to do with work.

A new report from ProPublica and The Texas Tribune shows that Paxton has taken almost 1,000 trips out of state since 2015, accompanied by Texas police each time at a cost of $3.3 million to his constituents. His security detail alone cost $24,000 a month, while his predecessor Greg Abbott’s cost $7,400 a month. Of those 1,000 trips, research only linked 138 of them to actual business. In fact, Paxton didn’t even record them as such.

Paxton took 53 trips to Florida, 24 trips to Utah—where his family trust owns properties—and 19 trips out of the country, all on the taxpayer’s dime. Paxton did not offer any specific explanation for his lack of business records for the trips.

“Throughout his career, Ken Paxton has faced numerous security threats stemming from his courageous work as Attorney General fighting on behalf of the people of Texas,” said his office in a statement. “Those threats are a direct result of him taking on the cartels terrorizing Texans and some of the nation’s most dangerous violent criminals.”

Beyond being a blatant misuse of public funds, especially given how many trips he took to his properties, this is a sign that Paxton cares more about his political office and its perks than he does about his actual constituents, who are paying for those perks.

“If you’ve got all these extra trips, it becomes ethically and morally problematic,” former National Association of Attorneys General executive director Chris Toth told ProPublica. “The ethical question is whether a legitimate security function has effectively become a taxpayer-funded subsidy.”

Paxton has been followed by crises of his own making for the entirety of his time as attorney general, as well as his candidacy for Senate. From his indictment and suspension to his alleged affair and subsequent divorce, and then his controversial, leak-filled Senate campaign, the GOP couldn’t have chosen a weaker candidate to field against James Talarico in Texas to defend its Senate majority.

items.title: If Dems Win, Inscribe This Chart on Trump-MAGA’s Political Gravestone
items.content_text:
With a bit of luck, this midterm election could finally break what we might call the Myth of Multiracial MAGA. That pervasive notion held that Trump’s 2024 gains with Latinos heralded the birth of a new multiethnic working-class coalition anchored around right-wing populist ideas. In the ultimate humiliation for liberals, that included immigration restrictionism.

A fresh blow to this notion came this week with an NBC poll finding Trump’s approval with Latinos sinking to 27 percent, and Democrats leading among them in the generic matchup by 59–35. But such polls capture only half the story. The other factor to consider? Latino turnout.

A new analysis by the Democratic data firm TargetSmart—which we obtained before its release—demonstrates something striking: As of right now, the Latino share of the early vote is dramatically outpacing where it was at the equivalent moment in both 2022 and 2024.

Here’s the truly wild finding: The raw number of early Latino votes is outpacing the raw total of them at the same point in 2024. That’s a surprise, because 2024 was a presidential year, when voter turnout is traditionally much higher, especially among nonwhites. Yet more Latinos have voted as of now—in this midterm—than at this point in the last presidential cycle.

TargetSmart’s analysis looked at the 229 counties across the country that are currently reporting early votes, mostly concentrated in states like Michigan, Ohio, Wisconsin, Virginia, New Jersey, and Florida.

Here’s the first key finding on vote share:

As you can see, as of October 8, Latinos comprise nearly 8 percent of the early vote in those 229 counties, substantially higher than the percentages in 2022 and 2024, per TargetSmart’s analysis. Those gains amount to big numbers, as the second key finding on raw vote totals shows:

That graphic is remarkable. As of October 8, according to the analysis, nearly 112,000 Latinos have voted, versus the approximately 106,000 who cast votes by the same time in the presidential year of 2024.

“While it’s still early, it’s incredibly unusual to see any group outperform presidential turnout at this point in the cycle,” Tom Bonier, a senior adviser at TargetSmart, told me. “Latino turnout tends to drop more in midterms. So seeing this early surge suggests we’ll potentially see historic levels of Latino engagement.”

What’s driving all this? The economy is likely the primary driver: The NBC poll found 74 percent of Latinos nationally disapprove of Trump’s handling of the economy. Latinos prefer Democrats to Republicans on the issue by 21 points—a huge turnaround from 2024, when Trump narrowly led Kamala Harris among Latinos on it.

But immigration also looms large. NBC finds 69 percent of Latinos disapprove of Trump’s handling of immigration and 58 percent disapprove on border security. Even the Republican pollster who helps conduct NBC’s poll says the issue is a big factor driving Latinos to Democrats.

Indeed, TargetSmart’s analysis also finds that many counties with the largest spikes in Latino turnout are also ones subjected to high-profile ICE activity. “Communities that have been directly impacted by ICE actions are generally seeing the largest increases in turnout,” Bonier said.

Here is a big caveat: We’re at the outset of early voting, so we’ll know more when early-vote tallies arrive from states like Texas, California, New York, and Pennsylvania, which will shed light on the Texas Senate races and many House races concentrated in those states.
